subject: Private Edge Appliance — outbound permitlist & firewall handoff
messages:
From: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: netops@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Permitlist for private edge appliance deployment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our security team we need a minimal, auditable outbound permitlist and firewall template for the Private Edge Appliance we'll host in our on-prem DMZ. The requirements are:

- Only permit outbound connections from the appliance's NAT egress IP(s) to a small set of Redwood endpoints.
- TLS 1.2+ and certificate validation required; mutual-TLS preferred for control-plane.
- DNS must resolve Redwood FQDNs internally; if we have to use proxy, we need FQDNs and SNI to be stable.
- Ports limited to 443 for HTTPS and 853/53 for DNS where needed; optional health-check port 9443 if you require it.

Can you send a CSV of exact IPs/FQDNs and a recommended firewall rule set we can hand to our NetOps team? Also indicate whether any endpoints are behind ephemeral IPs (rotation cadence) or require a TLS SNI allowlist.

We will track this in NETOPS-4123. Attached a blank template for permitlist.csv to fill.

Regards,
Alan
NetOps Manager
AcmeHealth
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Permitlist for private edge appliance deployment

Alan — thanks, great summary. Attaching our initial permitlist + network diagram. High level notes:

- Control plane endpoints (required for enrollment and audit log delivery):
  - control.redwood-inference.com (static set of egress IPs: 52.47.12.34, 34.201.98.22, 3.235.44.11) — these are stable / published.
  - mTLS is supported for control plane; we recommend enabling mTLS for the enrollment flow.

- Data-plane inference traffic (customer tenancy):
  - inference.redwood-inference.com — we support both IP-based allowlist and FQDN+SNI. Data-plane endpoints are behind a small rolling pool (rotation window ~48h). If you cannot allow a rotating IP set, permit by FQDN+SNI and validate certs.

- Telemetry and health checks:
  - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443) — optional, used for telemetry upload.
  - health.redwood-inference.com:9443 — only if you enable active health pings.

Firewall rule recommendations (minimal):
1) Source: APPLIANCE_PRIVATE_IP / NAT (apply on perimeter NAT) -> Dest: 52.47.12.34,34.201.98.22,3.235.44.11 Ports: 443 Protocol: TCP Purpose: Control-plane enrollment + audit
2) Source: APPLIANCE_PRIVATE_IP / NAT -> Dest: inference.redwood-inference.com Ports: 443 Protocol: TCP Purpose: Customer inference traffic (allow by FQDN+SNI where possible)
3) Source: APPLIANCE_PRIVATE_IP -> Dest: 8.8.8.8:53, 1.1.1.1:53 Protocol: UDP/TCP Purpose: DNS fallback (if you don't use internal DNS forwarders)
4) Deny all other outbound from appliance to Internet (explicit deny)

Notes on IP rotation and fallback:
- If your firewall can't do FQDN/SNI allowlisting, we can provide a short-lived snapshot of the active egress IPs for a manual allowlist. We'll mark that as an "ephemeral snapshot" and share via a signed Drive link.
- For customers requiring evidence: we can produce a signed manifest (CSV) with timestamped IPs and a short audit note. Kimberly will own that pack.

Next steps:
- I'll fill the permitlist CSV and you confirm with NetOps.
- Kimberly: can you add the audit-evidence process and point to the SOC2 artifact we can reference?
- Marissa: please add this to the deployment runbook and flag the SRE on-call for first 72h post-rollout.

Thanks — attaching permitlist_v1.csv and onprem-network-diagram-v2.png.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@acmehealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Permitlist for private edge appliance deployment

Alan — quick follow-up from network engineering perspective. A few clarifications so the handoff to your NetOps is frictionless: 

1) NAT behavior: ensure your perimeter NAT preserves source NAT mapping per appliance (we need stable outbound IP at least per appliance cluster). If you're using ephemeral NAT pools, please pin a small static egress IP for the appliance's subnet.
2) MTLS: if you enable mutual TLS for the control plane, we will provide client cert CNs to allow in your firewall/inspection logs (we don't require client IP-based allowlist in that case).
3) DNS: prefer allowing outbound to your internal resolver which forwards to public resolvers. If you require we can ESR (enterprise-safe) list Google/AWS resolvers.

I'll also attach a small snippet for a Palo Alto firewall (example) and an iptables excerpt for on-prem appliances.

-David
David Kim
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

If you can deliver the signed snapshot and the Palo Alto snippet by EOD Wednesday (US-PST) we can schedule the change on Thursday morning.

—Alan
